observations: Photo shows a dark screen TV with visible glare/reflection; no clear screen content.
No readable brand/model label is visible in the photo.
No clear view of the back panel, ports, power button, or any damage details.

claims.claim: A 29-inch LG TV is for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show any readable LG branding or the screen size.

claims.claim: It’s the transformer that got blown up.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows no internal/back view or component-level evidence; transformer failure cannot be confirmed remotely.

claims.claim: Location: Onike, near the University of Lagos (Unilag), Lagos State.
claims.evidence: No location evidence in the photo.

risks.risk: TV may have more than transformer damage (e.g., power supply board, main board, backlight/LED driver, panel damage).
risks.proof: A short video of the TV attempting to power on (standby light behavior) plus a clear photo of the back cover/label and any visible burnt parts on the power board.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / parts-only until proven otherwise.

risks.risk: Screen/panel may be damaged (no image, lines, or backlight issues).
risks.proof: Video showing power-on with brightness/backlight visible (even if no picture) and a close-up of the screen for lines/spotting.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / no guarantee of display.

risks.risk: Brand/model and exact size may be different from what’s claimed, affecting parts availability and value.
risks.proof: Photo of the TV’s rear label showing LG model number and screen size.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case generic broken TV value without assuming LG/29-inch.

risks.risk: Possible scam/incorrect item (photos don’t confirm the claimed model or fault).
risks.proof: Photo of the exact TV with a visible label + a photo of the power board area (back cover removed) showing the suspected transformer/power section.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the rear label (LG model number + screen size).
Photo of the back cover and power supply area (showing the transformer/power board).
Short video: plug in, power on, show standby light and any backlight/power behavior.
Close-up photo of the screen (for lines/spotting) and ports (to confirm completeness).
response.reason: From photo 0, the TV’s brand/model/size and the claimed transformer-only fault are not verifiable. With no proof of what’s actually damaged, the safest pricing requires confirmation via rear label and power-on/backlight behavior.
